# sq-19 — squalify must measure its throughput on GB-scale wide files

Adds a manual benchmark on generated GB-scale streams, including wide, right-padded fixed-width tables. It measures the three-pass design and records figures that inform any later decision to fuse passes. It changes no design by itself.

**2026-10-27** — From sq-06 architect (K7): reads per delimited file are ByteSniffer (full), TextScanner scoring (full), DelimitedPass (full), LineReader (re-decode from byte 0 to the last wanted line) and NameHex (prefix, only with U+FFFD). Worst cases are unbounded (long preamble, giant header line). DelimitedPass already gets byte offsets via IPhysicalLineSink.Line, so one seek-based head read, or capturing the header window during the pass, can serve LineReader and NameHex.

**2026-10-29** — Large run (2026-10-29), one run, alone, branch sq-19 at 336a5e6, command: SQUALIFY_BENCH_COMMIT=336a5e6 dotnet test tests/squalify.Tests/squalify.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ThroughputTests&Category=Large'. Machine class: macOS 26.3.0, arm64, 10 CPUs, .NET 10.0.14, workstation concurrent GC (serverGC=False), no GC env overrides. All 3 tests passed in 7.2 min. MB is 10^6 bytes; cells are data rows x columns; growth is peak working set minus a 1 MiB-stream baseline of the same shape; the ceiling is MemoryBudget.CeilingBytes for the pass.
PLAIN 12 columns, 1 GiB (10,737,418 rows, 128.8M cells; ASSERTED): read only 0.87 s (1229 MB/s); byte pass 1.75 s (615 MB/s), growth 1.1 MB vs ceiling 67.1 MB; full profile 84.1 s (12.8 MB/s, 1.53 Mcells/s), peak 79.3 MB, growth 7.1 MB vs ceiling 76.5 MB (estimate 9.4 MB).
PADDED WIDE 256 x 64, 1 GiB (64,527 rows, 16.5M cells; ASSERTED): read only 0.27 s; byte pass 2.32 s (463 MB/s), growth 1.8 MB vs 67.1 MB; full profile 71.7 s (15.0 MB/s, 0.230 Mcells/s), peak 216.0 MB, growth 145.6 MB vs ceiling 159.1 MB (estimate 92.0 MB; margin 13.5 MB, 91 percent of the ceiling).
PADDED WIDE 256 x 64, 4 GiB (258,111 rows, 66.1M cells; recorded, not asserted): read only 0.63 s; byte pass 9.04 s (475 MB/s); full profile 260.6 s (16.5 MB/s, 0.254 Mcells/s), peak 210.8 MB, growth 140.3 MB (below the 159.1 MB ceiling; estimate 92.0 MB).
Reading: memory growth levels off after the exact caps fill (140 to 146 MB at 1 and 4 GiB), no unbounded component; the 1 GiB wide margin is thin (13.5 MB), so a new per-field member that is not in EstimatedBytes would show up here first. The byte pass is about 2 to 3 percent of the full-profile time (2.3 s of 71.7 s; 1.7 s of 84.1 s), so the cost is in the later passes (scoring and the delimited pass), not in the byte pass. Per byte the full profile is similar for plain and padded (12.8 and 15.0 MB/s); per cell the wide shape is about 6.6 times slower, so at this size cost tracks bytes more than cells.
RECOMMENDATION (the owner decides): keep the three passes for 1.0.0. Fusing the byte pass into another pass could save at most about 3 percent. The benchmark did not time the scoring pass and the delimited pass separately, so it cannot say what fusing those two would gain; if the owner wants that decision, file an item to time them separately first.

**Not in this slice:** merging passes or other optimisation (a separate item if the figures call for it); parallel processing; speed checks in CI.

## Why

Goal: a full streaming scan with bounded memory, at the sizes real files reach.

Sample-data review (2026-10-13), adopted by the owner: production-test exports reach several GB with hundreds of columns, and about 90% of their bytes are padding. Processing cost tracks cells rather than bytes, and the design reads the file three times. Nobody has measured squalify on such a file.

## Files

- `tests/squalify.Tests/Sources/SyntheticCsvSource.cs` (from sq-11): adds a wide, padded mode: M columns of fixed width with right padding, a key preamble, annotation rows and a header, generated on the fly.
- `tests/squalify.Tests/Bench/ThroughputTests.cs`: `[Trait("Category","Large")]`, manual only. For a 1 GB stream, padded wide and plain, it records wall time, MB/s, cells/s and peak working set, for the byte pass alone and for the full profile, and asserts peak working set ≤ `MemoryBudget.CeilingBytes` (sq-11). `Bench_PaddedWide_4Gb` records the same figures for a 4 GB padded wide stream without asserting them; its figures go into the note only.
- A slicer note on this item with the figures, the machine class (no host names) and a recommendation: keep three passes, or file an item to fuse them.

## Failing tests

1. `SyntheticCsvSource_PaddedWide_ConstantLineLength`: every table line has the same length, and the profiler reports `constantLineLength`.
2. `Bench_PaddedWide_1Gb` and `Bench_Plain_1Gb` (Large): complete with peak working set ≤ `MemoryBudget.CeilingBytes` (sq-11).
